title: SLO-driven backpressure broker: adaptive retries, regional circuit-breakers, and idempotency SDK contract
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Problem: We observe tail-latency spikes and regional cascades during partial infra degradation (spot eviction events, transient AZ network flaps). Current retry and hedging behaviors are static and implemented ad-hoc across services and SDKs. This causes: increased cross-region traffic during failover, duplicated work for non-idempotent requests, and missed SLOs when burst traffic exhausts capacity.

Proposal: Build an SLO-driven Backpressure Broker service plus an SDK contract to standardize safe retry/hedge semantics and idempotency propagation. The broker will provide dynamic per-tenant and per-route retry budgets, regional circuit-breaker state, and adaptive load-shedding hints. SDKs will implement a small contract: explicit idempotency-key header semantics, a hedging window policy, and a retry-budget client token used to coordinate hedged requests with broker-derived budgets.

Goals:
- Reduce tail latency SLO breaches by coordinating retries and hedges with current capacity and SLO burn rate.
- Minimize cross-region amplified traffic during failovers using region-aware circuit breakers and controlled hedging.
- Ensure safe retries for non-idempotent operations via standardized idempotency token propagation and server-side guarantees.

Non-goals: Replace per-service local rate limiting for edge cases; fully centralize all traffic shaping (the broker is advisory and issues tokens/hints, enforcement remains at service edge).
acceptance_criteria: Backpressure Broker MVP deployed to staging with basic APIs: /budget, /circuit-state, /shed-hint
SDKs (python and js) implement idempotency-key header behavior and consume retry-budget tokens
Canary run shows 30% reduction in tail latency (p99) under synthetic partial-region degradation tests
Integration tests validate that hedged requests include the retry token and are suppressed when the broker returns budget=0
Runbook updated with triage steps for broker-induced shedding and metrics to monitor

decisions: Broker is advisory: services can opt-in to enforce tokens (edge-proxy will be the default enforcement point)
Idempotency key format: uuid v4 or deterministically derived hash; header name: X-Redwood-Idempotency
Hedging policy: SDK sends initial request plus one hedged request after 'hedge-window' ms only if budget token allows and circuit-state permits
Circuit-breakers are region-scoped and expose 'OPEN', 'THROTTLE', 'CLOSED' states with recommended shed-hint percentages
Retry-budget tokens are short-lived (TTL 5s) and include a numeric budget and a generation id to prevent stale acceptance
risks_and_mitigation: Single broker outage could bias shedding decisions: mitigate with regional replicas and client caching of last-known state
Incorrect idempotency usage by clients could cause silent duplication: mitigate with SDK helpers and server-side validation logs
Increased latency from broker exchange on hot paths: mitigate by making token exchange lazy and allowing cached local fallback decisions
notes: Benchmark notes: initial microbench shows broker token fetch adds ~0.7ms median when cached; worst-case cold fetch 3-5ms depending on region
Related work: aligns with multi-region failover runbook and circuit-breaker policy updates (see ENG-42911)
Follow-ups: expand to dedicated capacity policies for Reserved pools to avoid cross-tenant shedding
